# A statement line is generated by its reconciliation, one write edits a whole bank line, a statement is put in order from the paper, and a card statement is one statement

Shipped 2026-10-24 and 2026-10-25 · ⚠️ breaking · contract `0cd36b98415f5f0c` to `48ae0b6acb393dfa`
(everything after `f5cbc6ab4841f0a7`, the version you have read up to)

Answers: "One write edits a whole bank line: its line fields and its full set of parts" (raised
2026-10-24), in sections 6 and 7; "The statement order lists a statement's unplaced lines oldest
first", "A reconciliation's bank lines can be listed in the statement's order" and "A transaction
can be created straight into a reconciliation" (all three raised 2026-10-24), in sections 8, 9
and 10; "A reconciliation names its statement's other half and whether the statement is ordered",
"One write completes or reverts a whole statement, both halves of a card", "One write creates, or
deletes, both halves of a card statement" and "PUT on either half of a card moves the name and the
dates on both" (all four raised 2026-10-24), in sections 11–15. Sections 1–5 answer no ask: it is the owner's rule that a
statement line (`SIG-202603-029`, the sheet's `COD_EECC`) exists only because a reconciliation
made it, and it pairs with your own plan to stop sending `COD_EECC` as a statement line on import.

## Each ask

**"One write edits a whole bank line: its line fields and its full set of parts"**: done, with
these differences from the ask:

- **No `statement_line` in the body.** No client sends a statement line any more (section 1);
  `statement_line` and `statement_place` in the body are `422` (`UNKNOWN_FIELD`).
- **`POST /transactions/{id}/split` is removed** (the owner's decision): `PUT /bank-lines/{id}`
  with `parts` is the one way to rewrite a line's parts, with every rule and reason the split had.
  Your split screen moves to it (section 7).
- **A field left out of a kept part is unchanged**, as on `PUT /transactions/{id}`; the ask did
  not say. On a new part it takes the defaults (`@Pendiente`, the pending hashtag, no description).
- **`hashtag_ids` on a kept part always counts as a change**, as on `PUT /transactions/{id}`: that
  part is written (`version` bumps, an `updated` entry) even when the set is the one it has. A part
  sent with every value it has and no `hashtag_ids` is not written. So leave `hashtag_ids` out of
  any part whose hashtags the owner did not touch.
- **`null` on a kept part's `description` is `422`** (`NOT_NULL`), as on `PUT /transactions/{id}`;
  `""` empties it.
- **`PUT /transactions/{id}` keeps its line fields**: it still changes the title, date, account,
  operation code and reconciliation of the whole line, by the same rules as `PUT /bank-lines/{id}`.

**"The statement order lists a statement's unplaced lines oldest first"**: done as asked
(section 8). The tie-break, after the line's full date, is the time the line was created, then
its `line_code`. As you confirmed, two lines holding one place are now listed under it oldest
first too, so `places` and `unplaced` follow one rule.

**"A reconciliation's bank lines can be listed in the statement's order"**: done as
`GET /bank-lines?reconciliation_id=…&sort=statement` (section 9), accepted only with
`reconciliation_id`. `GET /bank-lines/count` is unchanged and takes no `sort`, since the order
does not change the count.

**"A transaction can be created straight into a reconciliation"**: done as asked (section 10),
plus one rule the ask did not mention: the items of one batch `line_group` name the same
reconciliation or none.

**"A reconciliation names its statement's other half and whether the statement is ordered"**:
done as asked (section 11), the second count named `shared_place_count`.

**"One write completes or reverts a whole statement, both halves of a card"**: done as asked
(section 12). The answer is the one you read today, for the half the path names, plus `twin`; the
other half's refusals are keyed with a `twin.` prefix; an archived account on either half refuses
the whole write.

**"One write creates, or deletes, both halves of a card statement"**: done, with one difference:
refusals come one check at a time, as on complete, not all in one answer (a taken id is `409` and
an overlapping period `422`, so they cannot share one answer). The create is `POST
/reconciliations` with `twin` (section 13); the delete is `DELETE /reconciliations/{id}` on either
half (section 14), and deleting one half of a card alone is no longer possible. `twin` reads `null`
on a reconciliation with no other half, and a create without `twin` is one half alone, as today;
the contract states both.

**"PUT on either half of a card moves the name and the dates on both"**: done as asked (section
15). `PUT /reconciliations/{id}` now answers with `twin` too, and moving one half's days alone is
no longer possible.

## What changed

### 1. No client sends a statement line (`0cd36b98415f5f0c`, breaking)

`statement_line` left every transaction write. `POST /transactions`, each item of
`POST /transactions/batch` and `PUT /transactions/{id}` refuse it, a value or `null`, as an
unknown field, and nothing is written.

Before (accepted, `201`):

```
POST /v1/transactions
{"id": "…", "account_id": "…", "amount_cents": -2500, "date": "2026-03-02T00:00:00-05:00",
 "statement_line": "SIG-202603-001"}
```

Now: `422`

```
{"error": {"code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "…",
  "fields": {"statement_line": "Extra inputs are not permitted"},
  "reasons": {"statement_line": "UNKNOWN_FIELD"}}}
```

In a batch the key is `transactions.<i>.statement_line`. `statement_line` stays on every read.
`STATEMENT_LINE_EXISTS` is no longer sent by any route. *Field locking* now freezes six fields
(`amount_cents`, `account_id`, `title`, `date`, `operation_code`, `reconciliation_id`), and an
archived account's transaction can no longer have a statement line filled in.

**Your live contract suite breaks:** its 8 tests that send `statement_line` on a transaction
write fail until they stop sending it. Your sheet import already sends none; keep using
`COD_EECC` there only to group the parts of a split into one line (`line_group` on the batch).

### 2. An account's statement code (`48d909f787839fa8`)

- `statement_code` on every account response, after `color`: the three-letter code of the
  account's bank product (`SIG`, `PEN`, `USD`, `ORO`), `null` when it has none.
- Optional on `POST /accounts`; set, changed or cleared (`null`) with `PUT /accounts/{id}`, on an
  archived account too. Exactly three capital letters `A`–`Z`, compared as sent; anything else
  (`sig`, `SI`, `S1G`, `" SIG"`) is `422` on `statement_code` (`INVALID_FORMAT`).
- **A card's two accounts share one code.** Two live accounts share a code only when their
  currencies differ: Visa Signature PEN and Visa Signature USD may both be `SIG`; a second PEN
  account with `SIG` is `409` on `statement_code` (`STATEMENT_CODE_EXISTS`).
- A person never carries one. `POST /people` does not take it (`422`, `UNKNOWN_FIELD`; its
  request is its own schema, `PersonCreateRequest`). `PUT /accounts/{id}` setting a code on a
  person is `422` on `statement_code` (`PERSON_ACCOUNT`). `POST /accounts/{id}/make-person` on an
  account with a code is `409` on `account_id` (`HAS_STATEMENT_CODE`): clear the code first.

### 3. One statement per code per month (`a1859d71873b8807`)

A reconciliation's statement month is the month of its `date_end`. Among the accounts sharing a
code, only one statement may end in a month. A card statement is **two reconciliations** (one on
each account) over **exactly the same days**: they are one statement, called twins. Each still
balances on its own, in its own currency.

- `POST /reconciliations` and `PUT /reconciliations/{id}`: a reconciliation that would clash is
  `422` on `date_end` (`STATEMENT_MONTH_TAKEN`), naming the clashing one and its days. Example:
  with `SIG` on both card accounts, a PEN reconciliation 2026-02-25..2026-03-25 and a USD one
  2026-02-25..2026-03-25 are both accepted; a USD one 2026-02-26..2026-03-25 is refused (same
  month, other days). Two reconciliations on one coded account ending in one month are refused
  too.
- `PUT /accounts/{id}` setting or changing a code is `422` on `statement_code`
  (`STATEMENT_MONTH_TAKEN`) when it would make two statements end in one month.
- Accounts without a code are unaffected.

### 4. A statement's order (`00c19334d476f25f`)

The engine cannot know the bank's order (the statement lists by processing date, which the ledger
does not store), so the client sends it once.

**`PUT /v1/reconciliations/{reconciliation_id}/statement-order`**, with `X-Idempotency-Key`,
from either half of a card:

```
{"places": ["<line 1 id>", "<line 2 id>", null, "<line 4 id>", …]}
```

The statement's **bank line** ids (`GET /bank-lines?reconciliation_id=…`), top to bottom as the
paper shows them, **both currencies mixed in one list** for a card. `null` is an empty slot for a
line the paper has and the ledger does not (a zero-amount fee), so the next line keeps the
paper's number. Each listed line's place is its position from 1. Answers `200` with the read
below.

Refused, nothing written, in this order:

| Status | Key | Reason | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `422` | `places` | `OUT_OF_RANGE` | 0 or more than 999 entries |
| `404` | | | not the caller's live reconciliation |
| `409` | `reconciliation_id` | `ACCOUNT_ARCHIVED` | either half's account is archived |
| `409` | `reconciliation_id` | `NO_STATEMENT_CODE` | the account has no statement code |
| `409` | | `CONCURRENT_CHANGE` | the statement's halves changed meanwhile: send again |
| `409` | `reconciliation_id` | `RECONCILIATION_NOT_DRAFT` | either half is completed: revert it first |
| `422` | `places.<i>` | `TRAILING_EMPTY_SLOT` | the list ends in `null` |
| `422` | `places.<i>` | `DUPLICATE_IN_REQUEST` | a line listed again (each later entry) |
| `422` | `places.<i>` | `LINE_NOT_IN_STATEMENT` | not a live line of this statement |
| `422` | `places.<i>` | `OPENING_BALANCE_NOT_PLACED` | an opening balance: leave it out |
| `422` | `places` | `STATEMENT_LINES_MISSING` | lines of the statement left out (named) |

The `422` problems come back together in one answer.

**`GET /v1/reconciliations/{reconciliation_id}/statement-order`**, from either half:

```
{"reconciliation_ids": ["<PEN half>", "<USD half>"],
 "places": [{"place": 1, "bank_line": {…as GET /bank-lines/{id}…}},
            {"place": 2, "bank_line": null}, …],
 "unplaced": [{…bank line…}, …]}
```

`places` runs from 1 to the highest place held; `bank_line` is `null` for an empty slot.
`unplaced` holds the statement's lines with no place (a line added after the order was sent, an
opening balance). `409 NO_STATEMENT_CODE` on an account without a code.

**`statement_place`** is new on every transaction response (after `statement_line`, also in
`changed_parts` and activity snapshots) and every bank line: the line's place, 1–999, `null` when
it has none. Every part of a line reads the same one. No request takes it.

A place stays only while the line stays in its reconciliation: `PUT /transactions/{id}` that
unassigns the line or moves it to another reconciliation sets it to `null`, and so does
`DELETE /reconciliations/{id}` (which may now also be `409 CONCURRENT_CHANGE` when an order is
sent at the same moment). A revert and a `parts` write (section 6) keep places. Nothing renumbers on its own: a line
added later has no place, and a line removed leaves its number unused, until a new list is sent.

### 5. The code itself (`206db22a65774501`)

`statement_line` is built by the engine on every read: `<CODE>-<YYYYMM>-<NNN>`, from the account's
statement code, the month of the reconciliation's `date_end` and the line's place, three digits.
It is `null` unless the line's reconciliation is **completed**, the line has a place and its
account has a code. Every statement line stored before is gone.

For a card statement whose paper shows rows 1–4 in soles, 5–6 in dollars, 7–8 in soles:

| Paper row | Account | `statement_line` once completed |
|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | Visa Signature PEN | `SIG-202603-001` … `SIG-202603-004` |
| 5–6 | Visa Signature USD | `SIG-202603-005`, `SIG-202603-006` |
| 7–8 | Visa Signature PEN | `SIG-202603-007`, `SIG-202603-008` |

- Each half shows its codes once **it** is completed: soles completed and dollars still a draft
  means the soles lines show codes and the dollar lines read `null`.
- A revert makes that half's codes `null`; completing again brings the same codes back without
  sending the order again.
- Changing the account's code changes every code it shows.
- Every part of a split line shows the line's one code.
- No two live lines ever read the same code.

**Completing needs the order.** `POST /reconciliations/{id}/complete` on an account with a code is
`422` on `statement_order` (`STATEMENT_NOT_ORDERED`) until every live line of the statement (both
halves of a card; opening balances excepted) has a place and no two share one. The message
counts the lines with no place and names any place held twice. An account without a code
completes as before.

**A completed half never joins another by a code change.** `PUT /accounts/{id}` setting or
changing a code that would make a reconciliation the twin of a completed one is `422` on
`statement_code` (`COMPLETED_STATEMENT_JOINED`). Revert the completed one first.

**Work through a card statement as one:** create both halves, assign their lines, send the order
once, then complete both. The engine still accepts a new half over the days of a completed one,
but that half cannot complete (`STATEMENT_NOT_ORDERED`) until the completed half is reverted and
the whole order is sent again (no order is accepted while either half is completed,
`RECONCILIATION_NOT_DRAFT`). Guide the owner so this never happens: when a card has two
accounts, create both halves together.

### 6. `PUT /bank-lines/{id}` edits a whole line in one write (`58d18ab42f4c09a2`, `dcda6e2de2883f1a`)

**`PUT /v1/bank-lines/{bank_line_id}`**, with `X-Idempotency-Key`. Every transaction response
carries its `bank_line_id`. All or nothing: if anything is refused, nothing is written.

```
{"title": "Tottus — semana", "date": "2026-10-11T12:00:00-05:00",
 "parts": [
   {"id": "<a live part's id>", "amount_cents": -7000},
   {"id": "<another live part's id>", "amount_cents": -2000, "category_id": "<id>"},
   {"id": "<a new UUID>", "amount_cents": -1000, "hashtag_ids": ["<id>"]}]}
```

- **Line fields**, each optional: `title`, `date`, `account_id`, `operation_code`,
  `reconciliation_id`. Each is taken exactly as `PUT /transactions/{id}` takes it and written onto
  every part: the same `null` rules, trimming, *Field locking*, *Archived accounts*, *Sealed
  periods*, assignment rules and refusal order. A refusal caused by one part names it:
  `"Part <id> of this bank line is the cause: …"`.
- **`parts`**, optional, is the line's complete new set, 1 to 500. Each part takes `id` and signed
  `amount_cents` (both required), and optionally `category_id`, `description` and `hashtag_ids`.
  Anything else is `422` on `parts.<i>.<field>` (`UNKNOWN_FIELD`), line fields included.
  - A live part's id **updates it in place**; it keeps its id. A field left out is unchanged.
  - A new id **creates a part** with the line's fields after the write.
  - A live part **left out is deleted**.
  - Any other taken id (another line's part, a deleted part, another user's record) is `409` on
    `parts.<i>.id` (`ID_EXISTS`). Parts never move between lines.
  - `parts` left out leaves the parts as they are.
- **The total.** Outside a completed reconciliation the parts may add up to a new total. Inside
  one, they must add up to the line's current total (`422`, `SPLIT_TOTAL_MISMATCH` on `parts` and
  every `parts.<i>.amount_cents`). Redistributing, adding and dropping parts stay allowed there.
- **Locked in a completed reconciliation:** the line fields, judged on the key, so do not send
  `title`, `date`, `account_id`, `operation_code` or `reconciliation_id` at all on such a line
  (filling an empty `title` or `operation_code` excepted). `amount_cents` inside `parts` is not
  locked.
- **Refused on `parts`:** a line holding an opening balance (`OPENING_BALANCE_NOT_SPLIT`), a line
  with a part on an archived account (`ACCOUNT_ARCHIVED`), and a line whose parts differ in
  account or date unless the same body sends the `date` and `account_id` that unify them
  (`SPLIT_LINE_PARTS_DIVERGE`).
- **Every refusal comes back together** where the rules allow, keyed by the field sent:
  `title`, `parts.<i>.amount_cents`, and so on.

**Answer** `200`: the line exactly as `GET /bank-lines/{id}` returns it after the write, plus:

```
"changed_parts": [{"transaction": {…}, "left_reconciliation": false}, …],
"created_part_ids": ["<new UUID>"],
"deleted_part_ids": []
```

`changed_parts` lists the kept parts whose line fields changed, as on `PUT /transactions/{id}`. A
replay with the same key answers the same JSON (its key order may differ); the same key with
another body is `409`.

### 7. The split route is removed (`76ea2d3a139c816e`, breaking)

`POST /transactions/{id}/split` is gone. Before (`201`, every part recreated with new ids):

```
POST /v1/transactions/<transaction id>/split
{"title": "Tottus", "parts": [{"id": "<new UUID 1>", "amount_cents": -6000},
                              {"id": "<new UUID 2>", "amount_cents": -4000}]}
```

Now that path is `404` (`NOT_FOUND`). Send instead, keeping the existing part's id:

```
PUT /v1/bank-lines/<bank_line_id>
{"parts": [{"id": "<the existing part's id>", "amount_cents": -6000},
           {"id": "<new UUID>", "amount_cents": -4000}]}
```

Differences from the split:
- One part is enough: `parts` takes 1 to 500, so going back to one part is one write.
- Kept parts keep their ids and history; only parts left out are deleted.
- `title` is a line field: in a completed reconciliation, sending it at all is `422` (`LOCKED`),
  even with the current value. The split accepted an unchanged title there.
- The opening-balance, archived and diverging refusals are keyed `parts`, no longer
  `transaction_id`.
- Messages no longer speak of a split: `"Duplicate id within parts."`,
  `"Bank line validation failed."`. The reason codes are the same.

### 8. A statement is listed oldest first (`6dd3b03e8c587e8c`)

`GET` and `PUT /reconciliations/{id}/statement-order` list `unplaced` **oldest first**. Before,
they came newest first. The order is the same from either half:

1. the line's `date` (a line is dated by its newest part, as on `GET /bank-lines`);
2. then the time the line was created;
3. then its `line_code`, ascending.

A card's soles and dollar lines are mixed by date, not grouped by half. Lines on one day at the
same instant (an import dates every row at midnight) fall to the time each line was created, then
to `line_code`, so the lines of one batch or one import keep the order they were made in.
Rewriting a line's parts does not move it. A line assigned after the last order was sent is
listed by its date among the others, not at the top.

Two lines holding one place in `places` are listed under it in the same order, oldest first.
Before, they were newest first. Which lines sit under which place does not change.

So "every placed line in its place, then `unplaced` as listed" is a starting suggestion that
follows the paper, and the owner moves only the exceptions.

### 9. `GET /bank-lines?sort=statement` (`9a53690f5d08341f`)

**`GET /v1/bank-lines?reconciliation_id=<id>&sort=statement`** lists that reconciliation's lines
in the statement order. Lines holding a place come first, by `statement_place` ascending. Then
come the lines holding none. Ties are listed oldest first, exactly as in section 8.

- On a card it lists only that half's lines, so the places have gaps where the other half's lines
  sit: `1, 2, 4, 5, …`, then the unplaced lines (`statement_place: null`).
- On an account without a statement code its lines hold no place and are listed oldest first.
- Paging by cursor is exact in this order, and every other filter of `GET /bank-lines` still
  applies.
- `sort=date_desc` is the order the list already had, and the default. A request without `sort`
  answers exactly as before, and its cursors still read.

Refused:

| Status | Key | Reason | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `422` | `reconciliation_id` | `REQUIRED` | `sort=statement` without `reconciliation_id` (`"Must be sent with sort=statement."`) |
| `422` | `unreconciled` | `CONFLICTING_PARAMETERS` | `sort=statement` with both `reconciliation_id` and `unreconciled=true`, as before |
| `422` | `sort` | `INVALID_FORMAT` | any value but `date_desc` and `statement` |
| `422` | `after` | `INVALID_CURSOR` | a cursor from one order sent with the other; the message names `sort` |
| `422` | `sort` | `UNKNOWN_PARAMETER` | `sort` on `GET /bank-lines/count` |

### 10. A transaction is created straight into a reconciliation (`41f2662b8c773063`)

`POST /v1/transactions` and each item of `POST /v1/transactions/batch` take an optional
`reconciliation_id`:

```
POST /v1/transactions
{"id": "<new UUID>", "account_id": "<the half's account>", "amount_cents": -1290,
 "date": "2026-03-04T00:00:00-05:00", "title": "Comisión",
 "reconciliation_id": "<the reconciliation being ordered>"}
```

`201`: the transaction answers with that `reconciliation_id` and `statement_place: null`. It is
filed under `@Pendiente` when no category is sent, as any create is. Its line is among the
reconciliation's lines in the same write. The new line has no place, so on a statement-coded
account the order is sent again before the statement completes.

- **Refused exactly as `PUT /transactions/{id}` refuses the same assignment**, with the same
  messages, on `reconciliation_id` (`transactions.<i>.reconciliation_id` in a batch). Nothing is
  written:

  | Reason | When |
  |---|---|
  | `INVALID_REFERENCE` | missing, deleted or another user's |
  | `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH` | on another account than the transaction's `account_id` |
  | `RECONCILIATION_COMPLETED` | completed |

- **Order of refusals:** a taken `id` still answers first. Then `account_id`, then
  `reconciliation_id`, then the sealed period, the category and the hashtags.
- **A batch `line_group`:** every item of one group names the same reconciliation, or none.
  Otherwise each differing item is `422` on `transactions.<i>.reconciliation_id`
  (`LINE_GROUP_FIELDS_DIFFER`), as for the group's account and date, and nothing is written.
- **A complete sent at the same moment:** either the create lands first and the complete judges
  the statement with the new line in it, or the complete lands first and the create is refused
  `RECONCILIATION_COMPLETED`.
- Omitted or `null`, a create answers exactly as before. `POST /transactions/import` and
  `POST /accounts/{id}/opening-balance` do not take it (`422`, `UNKNOWN_FIELD`).

### 11. Every reconciliation names its other half and says whether it is ordered (`84edab727350838e`)

Every reconciliation in every answer (`GET /reconciliations`, `GET /reconciliations/{id}` and
every write) carries three new fields, always present, worked out when read:

| Field | What it is | No statement code |
|---|---|---|
| `twin_id` | the statement's other half: the live reconciliation on the other live account holding the same statement code, over exactly the same days; `null` when there is none | `null` |
| `unplaced_count` | the statement's lines (both halves') with no place | `null` |
| `shared_place_count` | the places held by two or more lines | `null` |

```
GET /v1/reconciliations?account_id=<the soles card>
{"items": [{"id": "…", "name": "Mar 2026", "status": 1, …,
            "twin_id": "<the dollar half>", "unplaced_count": 2, "shared_place_count": 1}]}
```

- Both halves read the same counts. A line split into parts counts once; an opening balance is
  never counted. With a code and no twin, the counts cover that reconciliation alone.
- **Both `0` means the order is complete:** `POST …/complete` will not refuse
  `STATEMENT_NOT_ORDERED`. The counts and that refusal come from one rule, so they cannot
  disagree.
- The list reads all three for every row in the same request: no per-row read of the order.
- **A deleted account holds no code.** A reconciliation left on one reads all three `null`, and
  `GET`/`PUT …/statement-order` on it answer `409` `NO_STATEMENT_CODE`.

### 12. Complete and revert act on the whole statement (`a8974449335213dc`, breaking)

`POST /v1/reconciliations/{id}/complete` on either half of a card completes both halves in one
write; `POST …/revert` reverts both. **There is no way left to complete or revert one half of a
card alone.** A reconciliation with no twin, or on an account without a code, completes and
reverts as before.

- **A half already in the asked state is left as it is** (no `version` bump, no entry);
  completing completes whichever half is still a draft, reverting reverts whichever is
  completed.
- **One check at a time.** Complete's checks keep their order (`ENDING_BALANCE_REQUIRED`,
  `NO_TRANSACTIONS_ASSIGNED`, `SETTINGS_MISSING`, `UNASSIGNED_IN_PERIOD`, then
  `STATEMENT_NOT_ORDERED`); each runs on both halves before the next, and the first that fails
  answers naming every half it failed on. Nothing is written. A non-zero difference is still
  allowed.
- **`twin.` keys.** A key without the prefix is the half the path names; with `twin.` it is the
  other half. Both halves with no ending balance:

  ```
  422 {"error": {"code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", …,
       "fields": {"ending_balance_cents": "Must be entered before completing.",
                  "twin.ending_balance_cents": "Must be entered before completing."},
       "reasons": {"ending_balance_cents": "ENDING_BALANCE_REQUIRED",
                   "twin.ending_balance_cents": "ENDING_BALANCE_REQUIRED"}}}
  ```

  `statement_order` stays one key: the order belongs to the whole statement.
- **An archived account on either half** refuses the whole write: `409` `ACCOUNT_ARCHIVED` on
  `reconciliation_id` (the path half's account), `twin.reconciliation_id` (the other's), or both.
- **`409` `CONCURRENT_CHANGE`** on `reconciliation_id` when a twin forms or goes while the write
  takes hold of the statement (checked after the `404`, before `ACCOUNT_ARCHIVED`). Both routes
  now declare it.
- **The answer** is the one you read today for the path half, every field where it was, plus
  `twin`: the other half after the write, in the same shape (on complete with its own `warnings`
  and `coverage_gap`), with no `twin` of its own; `null` with no other half. Each half that
  changed has its own `version` bump and `updated` entry. `GET` reads carry `twin_id` only.

### 13. One create makes both halves (`dc2756b9f0afa5a5`, `82cb2eff9cca94ef`)

`POST /v1/reconciliations` takes an optional `twin`. The name and days are typed once; the twin
takes them:

```
POST /v1/reconciliations
{"id": "<new UUID>", "account_id": "<soles card>", "name": "Mar 2026",
 "date_start": "2026-02-26", "date_end": "2026-03-25",
 "beginning_balance_cents": -120000, "ending_balance_cents": -98000,
 "twin": {"id": "<new UUID>", "account_id": "<dollar card>",
          "beginning_balance_cents": -30000, "ending_balance_cents": null}}
```

`201`: the soles half, with `twin` holding the dollar half as created. Both read back naming each
other as `twin_id`. Each half gets its own `created` entry; one idempotency key covers the write.

- **`twin.account_id`** must be the other live account holding `account_id`'s statement code.
  Otherwise `422` `NOT_STATEMENT_PARTNER` on `twin.account_id` ("Must be the other account holding
  this account's statement code."): `account_id` with no code, the same account, or an account
  without the code. A `twin.account_id` that is missing, deleted, archived or another user's is
  `INVALID_REFERENCE` on `twin.account_id`, and a person `PERSON_ACCOUNT`, as for `account_id`,
  checked first.
- **`twin.id` equal to `id`** is `422` `DUPLICATE_IN_REQUEST` on `twin.id`; a taken `twin.id` is
  `409` `ID_EXISTS` on `twin.id`, at the same step as a taken `id`. `twin.ending_balance_cents` is
  optional; an unknown key inside `twin` is `422` `UNKNOWN_FIELD` (`twin.<key>`).
- **One check at a time.** The create's steps run on both halves, and inside the last one each
  rule (the account, the twin's account, an overlapping period, the statement month) runs on both
  halves before the next. The first that refuses answers naming every half it refused (`twin.id`,
  `twin.account_id`, `twin.date_start`, `twin.date_end`); nothing is written. For example, with
  the dollar card's days already taken by another of its periods:
  `422 {"twin.date_start": "PERIOD_OVERLAPS"}`, nothing created.
- **Without `twin`**, the create makes one reconciliation alone, exactly as before.
- **`twin` in the answer is always the reconciliation `twin_id` names** (`twin.id == twin_id`), or
  `null` when `twin_id` is. So a lone create over exactly the days of a reconciliation on the other
  card account answers that reconciliation as `twin`, unchanged by the write
  (`82cb2eff9cca94ef`).

### 14. A delete removes the whole statement (`2d593d0bff8ffc5e`, breaking)

`DELETE /v1/reconciliations/{id}` on either half of a card deletes both. **There is no way left
to delete one half of a card alone.** With no twin or no code it deletes as before.

- Each half unassigns its own lines and clears their places, as a delete did, and gets its own
  `deleted` entry; one idempotency key covers the write.
- **One check at a time**, each on both halves: `404`; `409` `CONCURRENT_CHANGE` (a twin formed or
  gone meanwhile); `409` `ACCOUNT_ARCHIVED` on `reconciliation_id` / `twin.reconciliation_id`;
  `409` `RECONCILIATION_NOT_DRAFT` on the same keys when a half is completed (revert it first);
  then, as before, `CONCURRENT_CHANGE` for a line placed in the statement meanwhile.
- **The answer** is today's plus `twin`: the other half as deleted, no `twin` of its own; `null`
  with no other half. Both read `twin_id: null` and both counts `0` (`null` without a code).
- A second delete of the same statement sent at the same moment waits and answers `404`, no longer
  `409`.

### 15. A `PUT` renames or moves the whole statement (`efaac89d8cdc2cde`, breaking)

`PUT /v1/reconciliations/{id}` on either half of a card writes `name`, `date_start` and
`date_end`, when sent, to both halves in one write. Both keep the same days, so they stay each
other's twin, and every line keeps its half and its place. **There is no way left to rename one
half of a card or move its days alone.**

```
PUT /v1/reconciliations/<the dollar half>
{"date_start": "2026-02-25", "date_end": "2026-03-25"}
```

`200`: the dollar half with the new days, `twin` holding the soles half with the same days.

- **Balances stay per half.** `beginning_balance_cents` and `ending_balance_cents` are the path
  half's only. A `PUT` sending only balances leaves the other half untouched (no `version` bump,
  no entry, its account and status not checked), and still answers `twin`.
- **One check at a time**, each on both halves, the other half keyed `twin.`: `404`;
  `CONCURRENT_CHANGE` (now declared); `ACCOUNT_ARCHIVED` (on the twin, each of `twin.name`,
  `twin.date_start`, `twin.date_end` sent); `LOCKED` on a completed half's days
  (`twin.date_start`, `twin.date_end`; `name` stays editable on a completed half); an empty name;
  then the period rules: `RANGE_INVERTED` once on `date_end`, `PERIOD_OVERLAPS` on each half's
  own account (`date_start`, `twin.date_start`), `STATEMENT_MONTH_TAKEN` (`date_end`,
  `twin.date_end`). The two halves moving together never refuse each other. Nothing is written
  on a refusal.
- **On a reconciliation with no twin**, the same order applies, so a completed one now answers
  `LOCKED` before an empty `name`. A day change may still make it the twin of another account's
  reconciliation; the answer's `twin` is then that reconciliation.
- **The answer** is today's plus `twin`, the reconciliation `twin_id` names after the write, no
  `twin` of its own; `null` with none. Each half written has its own `version` bump and `updated`
  entry.

## What the TUI does

1. **Catch up with the contract**, `f5cbc6ab4841f0a7` → `41f2662b8c773063`: `statement_code` on
   accounts, `statement_place` on transactions and bank lines, the two statement-order routes,
   and every new reason above (`STATEMENT_CODE_EXISTS`, `HAS_STATEMENT_CODE`,
   `STATEMENT_MONTH_TAKEN`, `NO_STATEMENT_CODE`, `TRAILING_EMPTY_SLOT`, `LINE_NOT_IN_STATEMENT`,
   `OPENING_BALANCE_NOT_PLACED`, `STATEMENT_LINES_MISSING`, `STATEMENT_NOT_ORDERED`,
   `COMPLETED_STATEMENT_JOINED`); `PUT /bank-lines/{id}` and its answer; the split route gone;
   `sort` on `GET /bank-lines`; `reconciliation_id` on `POST /transactions` and batch items, with
   `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH` and `RECONCILIATION_COMPLETED` now declared there. Then
   `41f2662b8c773063` → `48ae0b6acb393dfa`: `twin_id`, `unplaced_count` and
   `shared_place_count` on every reconciliation; `twin` on every reconciliation write's answer;
   `twin` on `POST /reconciliations`; `NOT_STATEMENT_PARTNER`; `CONCURRENT_CHANGE` now declared
   on complete, revert, `PUT` and `DELETE /reconciliations/{id}`; `DUPLICATE_IN_REQUEST` on the
   create; and every `twin.`-prefixed key.
2. **Stop sending `statement_line`** anywhere, the 8 live-suite tests first.
3. **Account form:** a statement-code field (three capital letters), shown on bank accounts only.
4. **Reconciliation of a card is one statement on screen:** the list reads one page and shows
   each card statement as one row from `twin_id`, with whether it still needs ordering from
   `unplaced_count` and `shared_place_count` (both `0` = ready to complete). No statement-order
   read per row, and no pairing of halves by code and days in the TUI.
5. **A screen to put a statement in order:** read `GET …/statement-order`, let the owner arrange
   the lines (both currencies) and insert empty slots, and send `PUT …/statement-order`. Show the
   owner a mockup first.
6. **Show `statement_line`** where the owner wants to see a line's place on its paper statement.
   The engine serves it; where it appears is for you and the owner to settle.
7. **The line editor saves with one `PUT /bank-lines/{id}`**: line fields and the full set of
   parts in one body. Send a kept part's `hashtag_ids` only when the owner changed its hashtags,
   and no line field on a line in a completed reconciliation unless the owner changed it.
8. **Move the split screen** onto the same `PUT`, keeping each existing part's id; stop calling
   `POST /transactions/{id}/split`.
9. **The order screen opens in date order:** the placed lines in their places, then `unplaced`
   as the engine lists it, with no sorting of your own.
10. **The reconciliation screen lists its lines in the paper's order** with
    `GET /bank-lines?reconciliation_id=…&sort=statement`, paging with the cursor it returns.
11. **"Create the missing line here"** sends one `POST /transactions` with the half's
    `account_id` and the reconciliation's `reconciliation_id`, then shows the new line as
    unplaced. There is no second write and no "created but left outside the statement" state.
12. **One form makes a card statement:** the name and days typed once, then each half's balances,
    sent as one `POST /reconciliations` with `twin`. Show refusals on the half their key names
    (`twin.` = the second half).
13. **Complete, revert, delete, rename and move a card statement with one write each**, on
    either half's id; read the other half from the answer's `twin`. Remove every "one half
    completed / created / deleted" state and its recovery step: the engine no longer allows it.

## Done when

1. Your contract holds `48ae0b6acb393dfa`, with every fixture field one this engine serves.
2. Your live contract suite passes against the live engine, none of its tests sending
   `statement_line`.
3. The owner sets `SIG` on both Visa Signature accounts from the TUI.
4. The owner orders one card statement on the new screen, completes both halves, and every line
   shows the code its paper row has.
5. The owner edits a line's date and re-splits it 60 + 40 into 70 + 30 in one save; both parts
   keep their ids, and nothing calls the split route.
6. The owner takes a two-part line back to one part in one save.
7. The owner opens a card statement's order screen and its unplaced lines come in the paper's
   date order, both currencies mixed.
8. The reconciliation screen of an ordered statement lists its lines in place order, then the
   unplaced ones.
9. The owner creates a missing line from the order screen in one save, and it lands in that
   statement, unplaced.
10. The reconciliation list shows each card statement as one row, with whether it needs
    ordering, from one page and no other read.
11. The owner creates a card statement from one form, then completes, reverts, renames or moves
    its days, and deletes it, each in one save, and never sees one half without the other.
